reading.body:
Booz Allen Hamilton holds 122 granted patents, and its recent grants are detection and security methods rather than AI models or compute hardware.

The recent titles cluster around finding things in data: image tampering, cross-domain alignment, network penetration testing, anomaly detection in mobile networks, multi-mode scanning. This is the applied end of AI, where models are used to classify, detect, and secure, not the end that trains frontier systems. The company's own description points the same direction, naming battle management, secure communications, encryption, and edge compute as the capabilities it acquired with Ultra I&C Mission Solutions.

For AI scaling, the relevant word in that list is edge. Edge compute means processing pushed toward sensors and platforms rather than concentrated in large data centers, which changes the power and building demand profile. It does not remove the constraint, because edge devices still need power and still need to be built, but it spreads the requirement instead of concentrating it. Nothing in this data quantifies that demand.

The data does not cover revenue, contract values, headcount, or how much of the business depends on AI work. It records eight SEC filings between May 2026 and August 2026, including a 10-K and a 10-Q, but not their contents. The patent count comes from a single applicant-phrase search of granted patents since 2001, so it undercounts anything filed under a different name and says nothing about pending applications.

profile_text.body:
Booz Allen Hamilton is a public company founded in 1914 and headquartered in Tysons, trading under the ticker BAH. On its website the company says it transforms missions with tomorrow's technologies to advance the country's most critical civil, defense, and national security priorities.

The site states that Booz Allen has completed its acquisition of the Ultra I&C Mission Solutions business, which now operates as the commercial product and solutions component of Booz Allen's defense technology business. The company describes complementary capabilities in battle management, secure communications, encryption, and edge compute, which it says will accelerate delivery of interoperable, mission-ready technologies for national security.

The record lists no tracked products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers for the company. Its SEC filing record shows CIK 0001443646.
